I am 55 this year. I have been farming these 8.2 mu since I was 25 — thirty years. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher. My household has five people. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so most days it is just my husband and me in the fields, though they come home for harvest and planting when we are short of hands.

With 8.2 mu, I must be careful. This year, I will plant winter wheat on 6.5 mu in mid-October, right after the summer maize comes off. The remaining 1.7 mu I will plant with cotton in late April. I thought about giving up cotton because my waist cannot take the picking like it used to, but cotton prices were decent last year, and my neighbor's girl promised to help pick in autumn for a share of the money. I cannot pass that up.

For the wheat: I trust improved seeds, not the most expensive kind, but the ones from the county seed station that I know. I will rotary till the maize stubble first, spread compound fertilizer as a base, then sow. At green-up and jointing, I will top-dress with urea. Counting everything, that is about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. I will irrigate three times from my well: the winter irrigation before the ground freezes, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. Electricity for the pump costs money, so three times is my limit. I will spray pesticide twice — once for weeds and once if I see aphids. If the spring rain does not fail me, I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For the summer maize: Time is short after wheat harvest in mid-June. I will direct-seed hybrid maize into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. There is no time to plough, and I have learned from my neighbors that it works fine if you manage the straw. I apply about 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium, some at planting and some at the big喇叭口 stage. I irrigate twice — once when the tassels come out and once at filling if July is hot and dry. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 1.7 mu: Cotton needs deep, loose soil, so I plough in April. I use hybrid cotton seeds. I fertilize lighter than grain — about 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. But cotton needs more medicine. I will spray four times for bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite. I irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. I expect around 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

This is my plan. It is not new or clever, but it has fed my family for thirty years, and this year it will do the same.
